rute-sem-rute-03-mara-01.question: In Ruth 1:20, Naomi asked to be called Mara because of her great bitterness.
rute-sem-rute-03-mara-01.feedbackCorrect: She changes her name and explains why: great bitterness.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Ruth 1:20: she asks for the name and gives the reason herself.

rute-sem-rute-03-mara-01.hint: Look at the name she chooses for herself.

rute-sem-rute-03-mara-02.question: In Ruth 1:20, tap the name Naomi asks to be called.
rute-sem-rute-03-mara-02.feedbackCorrect: She asks for a name that reflects her bitterness.

feedbackWrong.b: That is her former name, which she rejects here.
feedbackWrong.c: That is God, whom she says caused her bitterness.

rute-sem-rute-03-mara-02.hint: It is the bitter name she chooses herself.

rute-sem-rute-03-mara-03.question: According to Ruth 1:21, how does Naomi say she left and how did she return?
rute-sem-rute-03-mara-03.feedbackCorrect: She left full and returned empty to Bethlehem.

feedbackWrong.a: It is the opposite: full when she left, empty when she returned.
feedbackWrong.c: Her sons died in Moab; she returns with Ruth.
feedbackWrong.d: Illness and healing are not mentioned in her words.

rute-sem-rute-03-mara-03.hint: Pay attention to the two contrasting words.

options.a: She left empty and returned with possessions
options.b: She left full and returned empty
options.c: She left alone and returned with her sons
options.d: She left sick and returned healed to Bethlehem

rute-sem-rute-03-mara-04.question: Put Ruth 1:21 in the order of the text.
rute-sem-rute-03-mara-04.feedbackCorrect: Full when she left, empty when she returned, then her feelings about God.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with how she was when she left.

rute-sem-rute-03-mara-04.hint: Her statement begins with her past.

rute-sem-rute-03-mara-05.question: In Ruth 1:21, what word does Naomi use to describe how she left Bethlehem?
rute-sem-rute-03-mara-05.feedbackCorrect: She left with her husband and sons: she left with a full family.

feedbackWrong.a: Empty describes how she returned, not how she left.
feedbackWrong.c: She left with her family, not alone.

rute-sem-rute-03-mara-05.hint: It is the opposite of how she returned.

rute-sem-rute-03-mara-06.question: What does Ruth 1:20 communicate that connects to this context?
rute-sem-rute-03-mara-06.feedbackCorrect: The new name expresses the pain of returning with nothing and no one.

feedbackWrong.a: She speaks to the women instead of hiding from them.
feedbackWrong.c: She does not celebrate wealth; she mourns her loss.

rute-sem-rute-03-mara-06.hint: Look at the feeling she expresses herself.

options.a: Shame at being recognized
options.b: The bitterness of returning empty
options.c: The joy of returning wealthy

rute-cam-rute-03-mara-01.question: In Ruth 1:20–21, Naomi connects the name Mara to what she feels the Almighty has done to her.
rute-cam-rute-03-mara-01.feedbackCorrect: The name comes from how she interprets her own loss.

feedbackWrong.false: She explains the name herself: the Almighty has caused her bitterness.

rute-cam-rute-03-mara-01.hint: Look for the explanation she gives for the name.

rute-cam-rute-03-mara-02.question: In Ruth 1:21, tap the word that contrasts how she left and how she returned.
rute-cam-rute-03-mara-02.feedbackCorrect: Full when she left, empty when she returned: this little word contrasts the two.

feedbackWrong.a: That word refers to God; it does not contrast leaving and returning.
feedbackWrong.b: That word appears in the women's question, without making a contrast.

rute-cam-rute-03-mara-02.hint: Look for the conjunction that contrasts full and empty.

rute-cam-rute-03-mara-03.question: Why does Naomi reject her former name in Ruth 1:20–21?
rute-cam-rute-03-mara-03.feedbackCorrect: In her view, her former name no longer fits the person who returned empty.

feedbackWrong.a: The text mentions no prohibition on names.
feedbackWrong.b: The women are actually using her former name.
feedbackWrong.d: Ruth does not speak in this welcoming scene.

rute-cam-rute-03-mara-03.hint: Compare how she left with how she returned.

options.a: Because Hebrew names were forbidden in Moab
options.b: Because the women were already using another name
options.c: Because she left with everything and returned with nothing
options.d: Because Ruth asked her to change her name

rute-cam-rute-03-mara-04.question: How do the statements in Ruth 1:20–21 unfold?
rute-cam-rute-03-mara-04.feedbackCorrect: Rejection, new name, and explanation: this is the order of her words.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with her rejection of the former name.

rute-cam-rute-03-mara-04.hint: The explanation comes after the new name.

options.a: She refuses to be called by her former name
options.b: She asks for a name that means bitter
options.c: She explains that she returned empty

rute-cam-rute-03-mara-05.question: In Ruth 1:21, how does Naomi say the Lord brought her back?
rute-cam-rute-03-mara-05.feedbackCorrect: She returned without a husband, sons, or support.

feedbackWrong.a: God is precisely the one she says brought her back.
feedbackWrong.c: Honor is what she feels she lost along the way.

rute-cam-rute-03-mara-05.hint: It is the opposite of having left full.

rute-cam-rute-03-mara-06.question: What connects Ruth 1:20 to Psalms 13:1?
rute-cam-rute-03-mara-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, pain becomes words directed to God, not silence.

feedbackWrong.b: Neither remains silent: both speak to God about their pain.
feedbackWrong.c: Pain is still present in both texts.

rute-cam-rute-03-mara-06.hint: Look at what both texts do with pain.

options.a: Lament that speaks to God
options.b: Silence in the face of suffering
options.c: Celebration at the end of pain

rute-pro-rute-03-mara-01.question: Ruth 1:20–21 teaches that Naomi lost her faith and abandoned the God of Israel.
rute-pro-rute-03-mara-01.feedbackCorrect: She laments before God; she does not stop speaking about him or turn away from him.

feedbackWrong.true: She returns to God's people and speaks about him: this is lament, not abandonment.

rute-pro-rute-03-mara-01.hint: See whether she stops speaking about God.

rute-pro-rute-03-mara-02.question: In Ruth 1:20, tap what Naomi says the Almighty caused her.
rute-pro-rute-03-mara-02.feedbackCorrect: This is the feeling that explains her new name.

feedbackWrong.a: This introduces her rejection of the name without naming the feeling.
feedbackWrong.b: This is her request, not what God caused her.

rute-pro-rute-03-mara-02.hint: Look for the feeling at the end of the verse.

rute-pro-rute-03-mara-03.question: What understanding of Naomi's bitterness does Ruth 1:20–21 support?
rute-pro-rute-03-mara-03.feedbackCorrect: She tells God how she feels, even through her name: this is lament.

feedbackWrong.a: Ruth is not blamed for anything in Naomi's words.
feedbackWrong.c: The text preserves her lament without condemning it.
feedbackWrong.d: She speaks of the Lord throughout; she does not deny God.

rute-pro-rute-03-mara-03.hint: Look at whom she speaks to about her pain.

options.a: She blames Ruth for everything she lost
options.b: She names her pain before God without stopping speaking about him
options.c: She teaches that lamenting is a lack of faith
options.d: She denies that God exists after her loss

rute-pro-rute-03-mara-04.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of Ruth 1:21–22?
rute-pro-rute-03-mara-04.feedbackCorrect: The scene of greatest pain ends precisely at the time of the harvest.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with her leaving full; the harvest closes the scene.

rute-pro-rute-03-mara-04.hint: The harvest season is the final detail.

options.a: She left Bethlehem with her family and everything she had
options.b: She returns empty and asks for another name
options.c: She arrives at the beginning of the barley harvest

rute-pro-rute-03-mara-05.question: In Ruth 1:21, what name does Naomi question people still calling her?
rute-pro-rute-03-mara-05.feedbackCorrect: To her, her former name no longer fits the person who returned.

feedbackWrong.b: This describes how she left; it is not a name.
feedbackWrong.c: That is the new name she requests, not the one she questions.

rute-pro-rute-03-mara-05.hint: It is the name she had before her loss.

rute-pro-rute-03-mara-06.question: What connects Ruth 1:20 to Exodus 15:23?
rute-pro-rute-03-mara-06.feedbackCorrect: In Exodus, Mara is the place of bitter water that could not be drunk.

feedbackWrong.a: Neither text mentions any wine.
feedbackWrong.c: Both involve a journey, but the connection is in the name.

rute-pro-rute-03-mara-06.hint: Compare the name in both texts.

options.a: Water turned into wine
options.b: Mara, the name of the bitter waters
options.c: A journey through the desert

rute-sem-rute-04-asas-01.question: In Ruth 2:12, Boaz asked the Lord to reward Ruth for her actions.
rute-sem-rute-04-asas-01.feedbackCorrect: He asks the Lord to repay and reward her.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Ruth 2:12: this is exactly what Boaz asks.

rute-sem-rute-04-asas-01.hint: Look at the request Boaz makes to God.

rute-sem-rute-04-asas-02.question: In Ruth 2:12, tap what Ruth sought refuge under.
rute-sem-rute-04-asas-02.feedbackCorrect: The image is of a bird covering her: refuge beneath its wings.

feedbackWrong.b: Israel is the people; the shelter is described with another image.
feedbackWrong.c: The Lord is the one who shelters her; the image comes afterward.

rute-sem-rute-04-asas-02.hint: Look for the image of covering at the end of the verse.

rute-sem-rute-04-asas-03.question: According to Ruth 2:11, what had people told Boaz about Ruth?
rute-sem-rute-04-asas-03.feedbackCorrect: Her reputation was based on her loyalty to her mother-in-law after the loss.

feedbackWrong.a: Marriage is not mentioned in what people told Boaz.
feedbackWrong.c: No one praised her for harvesting; the subject is her mother-in-law.
feedbackWrong.d: She did the opposite: she stayed with Naomi for good.

rute-sem-rute-04-asas-03.hint: Look at whom her loyalty was directed toward.

options.a: That she wanted to marry a rich man
options.b: What she did for her mother-in-law after becoming a widow
options.c: That she was Bethlehem's best harvest worker
options.d: That she planned to return to Moab

rute-sem-rute-04-asas-04.question: Put Ruth 2:11 in the order of the text.
rute-sem-rute-04-asas-04.feedbackCorrect: Parents, homeland, and a new people: this is the order of what she left behind.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the parents she left in Moab.

rute-sem-rute-04-asas-04.hint: The statement begins with what she left behind.

rute-sem-rute-04-asas-05.question: In Ruth 2:11, for whom did Ruth do everything that people told Boaz about?
rute-sem-rute-04-asas-05.feedbackCorrect: The loyalty that reached Boaz's ears was directed toward her mother-in-law.

feedbackWrong.a: No sister is mentioned in Boaz's account.
feedbackWrong.b: She left her mother in Moab; her loyalty was to her mother-in-law.

rute-sem-rute-04-asas-05.hint: She is the woman Ruth accompanied to Bethlehem.

rute-sem-rute-04-asas-06.question: What does Ruth 2:12 communicate that connects to this context?
rute-sem-rute-04-asas-06.feedbackCorrect: Boaz sees her coming as a search for shelter in the God of Israel.

feedbackWrong.a: Boaz speaks of a reward from the Lord, not a salary.
feedbackWrong.b: She did not return; she sought refuge and stayed.

rute-sem-rute-04-asas-06.hint: Look at the image Boaz uses at the end.

options.a: Work rewarded with wages
options.b: A repentant return to Moab
options.c: Refuge under God's wings

rute-cam-rute-04-asas-01.question: In Ruth 2:11–12, Boaz asked for a reward for Ruth because she was not a foreigner in Bethlehem.
rute-cam-rute-04-asas-01.feedbackCorrect: She was indeed a foreigner: she came to a people she did not know.

feedbackWrong.true: The text emphasizes that she left her homeland: she was an outsider.

rute-cam-rute-04-asas-01.hint: Remember where Ruth came from, according to Boaz.

rute-cam-rute-04-asas-02.question: In Ruth 2:11, tap the verb that summarizes what Ruth did with her former life.
rute-cam-rute-04-asas-02.feedbackCorrect: Her father, mother, and homeland were left behind: she left them all.

feedbackWrong.b: This refers to the news that reached Boaz, not to her actions.
feedbackWrong.c: This describes the new people, not what she did.

rute-cam-rute-04-asas-02.hint: Look for the action she took regarding her parents.

rute-cam-rute-04-asas-03.question: How does Ruth 2:12 interpret what Ruth did in Ruth 2:11?
rute-cam-rute-04-asas-03.feedbackCorrect: Leaving everything behind becomes, in Boaz's words, a search for shelter in God.

feedbackWrong.a: Boaz asks that the Lord be the one to reward her.
feedbackWrong.b: It is not luck; it is refuge sought in the God of Israel.
feedbackWrong.c: No custom is mentioned; Boaz speaks of her God.

rute-cam-rute-04-asas-03.hint: Look at the theological image Boaz uses.

options.a: As a debt Naomi would have to repay
options.b: As the luck of someone who found a good field
options.c: As a common custom among Moabite daughters-in-law
options.d: As a search for refuge in the God of Israel

rute-cam-rute-04-asas-04.question: How do the events in Ruth 2:11–12 unfold?
rute-cam-rute-04-asas-04.feedbackCorrect: News, recognition, and blessing: this is the order of his words.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with what reached Boaz's ears.

rute-cam-rute-04-asas-04.hint: The blessing is the final part of his statement.

options.a: People told Boaz what she had done for her mother-in-law
options.b: He recalls that she left her parents and homeland
options.c: He asks the God of Israel to reward her

rute-cam-rute-04-asas-05.question: In Ruth 2:12, what does Boaz ask the Lord to do for Ruth's actions?
rute-cam-rute-04-asas-05.feedbackCorrect: Boaz does not repay her himself; he asks the Lord to do so.

feedbackWrong.b: Hiding is not mentioned in Boaz's request.
feedbackWrong.c: He asks for the opposite: that her actions be repaid.

rute-cam-rute-04-asas-05.hint: It is the first thing he asks the Lord to do.

rute-cam-rute-04-asas-06.question: What connects Ruth 2:12 to Psalms 91:4?
rute-cam-rute-04-asas-06.feedbackCorrect: The psalm uses the same image: shelter under his wings.

feedbackWrong.b: Neither text speaks of guarding fields.
feedbackWrong.c: The image is not about real birds or harvesting.

rute-cam-rute-04-asas-06.hint: Compare the image of protection in both texts.

options.a: Refuge under God's wings
options.b: Widows guarding the field
options.c: Birds announcing the harvest

rute-pro-rute-04-asas-01.question: Ruth 2:11–12 teaches that God only welcomes under his wings those born among the people of Israel.
rute-pro-rute-04-asas-01.feedbackCorrect: The one who sought refuge was a Moabite, an outsider.

feedbackWrong.true: The welcome here is precisely for a foreign woman who sought refuge.

rute-pro-rute-04-asas-02.question: In Ruth 2:12, tap the phrase that shows Ruth's initiative in seeking shelter in God.
rute-pro-rute-04-asas-02.feedbackCorrect: She did not stumble upon refuge; she sought it when she came.

feedbackWrong.a: This refers to the one who shelters her; her search appears in another phrase.
feedbackWrong.b: This is what will be repaid, not the act of seeking refuge itself.

rute-pro-rute-04-asas-02.hint: Look for the verb that has Ruth as its subject.

rute-pro-rute-04-asas-03.question: What understanding of Ruth under God's wings does Ruth 2:11–12 support?
rute-pro-rute-04-asas-03.feedbackCorrect: Though she came from outside the people, she is welcomed into the shelter of their God.

feedbackWrong.a: Her faith is in the God of Israel, not something Boaz owns.
feedbackWrong.b: Wings are an image of care, not literal physical protection.
feedbackWrong.c: She continues gathering grain in the field: refuge does not eliminate work.

rute-pro-rute-04-asas-03.hint: Connect her origins with the image Boaz uses.

options.a: Boaz becomes the owner of Ruth's faith
options.b: God protects with physical wings those who work well
options.c: Those who find refuge in God do not need to work
options.d: The foreign woman is welcomed into the refuge of the God of Israel

rute-pro-rute-04-asas-04.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of Ruth 2:11–12?
rute-pro-rute-04-asas-04.feedbackCorrect: Leaving things behind, seeking refuge, and the requested reward: this is her path toward God.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with what she left behind in Moab.

rute-pro-rute-04-asas-04.hint: The requested reward completes the sequence.

options.a: She leaves her father, mother, and homeland
options.b: She seeks refuge in the God of Israel
options.c: Boaz asks the Lord for a full reward

rute-pro-rute-04-asas-05.question: In Ruth 2:12, what does Boaz ask the Lord to give Ruth?
rute-pro-rute-04-asas-05.feedbackCorrect: Boaz asks that her reward come from the Lord himself.

feedbackWrong.a: She has already made the journey; the request is for something else.
feedbackWrong.c: Bitterness is Naomi's word, not Boaz's request.

rute-pro-rute-04-asas-05.hint: It is what corresponds to her actions.

rute-pro-rute-04-asas-06.question: What connects Ruth 2:12 to Matthew 23:37?
rute-pro-rute-04-asas-06.feedbackCorrect: Jesus uses the same image: gathering the children under his wings.

feedbackWrong.b: Jesus laments their refusal; he does not announce such an ending.
feedbackWrong.c: The hen is an image of care, not the literal subject.

rute-pro-rute-04-asas-06.hint: Look at the image Jesus uses for Jerusalem.

options.a: Jesus gathers them under his wings
options.b: The end of the people of Israel
options.c: A hen lost in the field

rute-sem-rute-05-capa-01.question: In Ruth 3:11, Boaz promised to do everything Ruth said.
rute-sem-rute-05-capa-01.feedbackCorrect: These are his words: I will do everything you have said.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Ruth 3:11: this is exactly what Boaz promises.

rute-sem-rute-05-capa-01.hint: Look at the commitment he makes.

rute-sem-rute-05-capa-02.question: In Ruth 3:9, tap who Ruth says Boaz is to the family.
rute-sem-rute-05-capa-02.feedbackCorrect: It is because of his role as a relative that she asks him for protection.

feedbackWrong.a: Servant is how she introduces herself, not who he is.
feedbackWrong.c: That is her name, not his role.

rute-sem-rute-05-capa-02.hint: Look for the family relationship at the end of the verse.

rute-sem-rute-05-capa-03.question: According to Ruth 3:9, what did Ruth ask Boaz for at the threshing floor?
rute-sem-rute-05-capa-03.feedbackCorrect: She asks for the protection of her kinsman-redeemer.

feedbackWrong.a: She will receive barley, but her request here is for protection.
feedbackWrong.b: She speaks for herself, face to face with him.
feedbackWrong.c: Hiding is not what she asks for; she asks for a commitment.

rute-sem-rute-05-capa-03.hint: Look at the gesture she asks him to make over her.

options.a: To give her more barley to take home
options.b: To speak to Naomi on her behalf
options.c: To hide her until morning
options.d: To spread his cloak over her

rute-sem-rute-05-capa-04.question: Put Ruth 3:10 in the order of the text.
rute-sem-rute-05-capa-04.feedbackCorrect: Blessing, praise for her kindness, and the reason: this is the order of his words.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the blessing he speaks over her.

rute-sem-rute-05-capa-04.hint: His statement begins with a blessing over her.

rute-sem-rute-05-capa-05.question: In Ruth 3:9, what does Ruth ask Boaz to spread over her?
rute-sem-rute-05-capa-05.feedbackCorrect: Spreading this over someone was a sign of commitment.

feedbackWrong.a: The hand is not mentioned in her request that night.
feedbackWrong.b: Shadow is an image from the Psalms, not the word of this scene.

rute-sem-rute-05-capa-05.hint: It is a piece of his clothing.

rute-sem-rute-05-capa-06.question: What does Ruth 3:11 communicate that connects to this context?
rute-sem-rute-05-capa-06.feedbackCorrect: She asks for the covering of the one who can redeem the family.

feedbackWrong.b: She is not saying goodbye: she is asking for commitment.
feedbackWrong.c: She already had work in the field; the request is something else.

rute-sem-rute-05-capa-06.hint: See the basis she gives for her request.

options.a: Request for the redeemer's covering
options.b: Farewell before returning
options.c: Request for more work

rute-cam-rute-05-capa-01.question: In Ruth 3:10–11, Boaz agreed to help because Ruth went looking for the rich young men of Bethlehem.
rute-cam-rute-05-capa-01.feedbackCorrect: He praises precisely the opposite: she did not run after young men.

feedbackWrong.true: Boaz says she did not follow young men, poor or rich.

rute-cam-rute-05-capa-01.hint: See what she did not do, according to Boaz.

rute-cam-rute-05-capa-02.question: In Ruth 3:10, tap the little word that gives the reason for Boaz's praise.
rute-cam-rute-05-capa-02.feedbackCorrect: The praise has a reason: she did not seek just any young man.

feedbackWrong.b: Young man is whom she did not seek, not the reason itself.
feedbackWrong.c: Rich describes the young men, without explaining the praise.

rute-cam-rute-05-capa-02.hint: Look for the short conjunction in the middle of the sentence.

rute-cam-rute-05-capa-03.question: How does Ruth 3:10 explain Ruth's last kindness, better than the first?
rute-cam-rute-05-capa-03.feedbackCorrect: Before, loyalty to her mother-in-law; now, loyalty to the family's future.

feedbackWrong.a: No gift is mentioned in his speech.
feedbackWrong.b: The plan came from Naomi herself, with no secret on her part.
feedbackWrong.d: Hours of work are not the subject of the praise.

rute-cam-rute-05-capa-03.hint: Compare her two loyalties in his speech.

options.a: She brought expensive gifts to Boaz's house
options.b: She hid the plan of that night from Naomi
options.c: She sought the family's redemption, not just any young man
options.d: She worked more hours than on the first day

rute-cam-rute-05-capa-04.question: How do the events of Ruth 3:9–11 chain together?
rute-cam-rute-05-capa-04.feedbackCorrect: Request, blessing, and promise: that is the order of the conversation.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with her request on the threshing floor.

options.a: She presents herself and asks for covering
options.b: He blesses her for her loyalty
options.c: He promises to do what she said

rute-cam-rute-05-capa-05.question: In Ruth 3:11, what does Boaz say he will do with everything Ruth said?
rute-cam-rute-05-capa-05.feedbackCorrect: It is not perhaps: he commits himself to act.

feedbackWrong.a: He does not postpone to think: he promises to act.
feedbackWrong.c: Telling the city is not the promise he makes.

rute-cam-rute-05-capa-05.hint: It is a commitment, not a doubt.

rute-cam-rute-05-capa-06.question: What links Ruth 3:9 to Ezekiel 16:8?
rute-cam-rute-05-capa-06.feedbackCorrect: In Ezekiel, God spreads the cloak as a sign of covenant.

feedbackWrong.b: The cold of the night is not the meaning of the gesture.
feedbackWrong.c: It is not a gift of clothing: it is a sign of commitment.

rute-cam-rute-05-capa-06.hint: See what the gesture means in both texts.

options.a: Cloak spread as commitment
options.b: Cold during the night on the threshing floor
options.c: New clothes for a feast

rute-pro-rute-05-capa-01.question: Ruth 3:10–11 shows Boaz taking up Ruth's request with a clear promise, not out of a hidden impulse.
rute-pro-rute-05-capa-01.feedbackCorrect: He blesses, recognizes her worth, and promises to act.

feedbackWrong.false: His response is open and committed, not an impulse.

rute-pro-rute-05-capa-01.hint: See how he responds to her request.

rute-pro-rute-05-capa-02.question: In Ruth 3:11, tap who, according to Boaz, knows Ruth's worth.
rute-pro-rute-05-capa-02.feedbackCorrect: Her reputation is public, not a secret of the threshing floor.

feedbackWrong.a: That is how he calls her, not who knows her worth.
feedbackWrong.c: That is what they know about her, not who knows.

rute-pro-rute-05-capa-02.hint: Look for the subject who knows, at the beginning of the sentence.

rute-pro-rute-05-capa-03.question: What reading does Ruth 3:10–11 support about the threshing floor scene?
rute-pro-rute-05-capa-03.feedbackCorrect: Request for redemption, blessing, and promise: it is commitment, not scandal.

feedbackWrong.b: The city already knows her worth; there is no shame.
feedbackWrong.c: The request is for family redemption, with a stated reason.
feedbackWrong.d: He protects her and promises to act openly, in the morning.

rute-pro-rute-05-capa-03.hint: See the reason she herself declares.

options.a: She asks the relative for redemption and he accepts the task
options.b: The two hide a shameful plan from the city
options.c: She set up a seduction to trap Boaz
options.d: Boaz took advantage of her during the night

rute-pro-rute-05-capa-04.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of Ruth 3:9–13?
rute-pro-rute-05-capa-04.feedbackCorrect: Request, recognition, and responsible action: the redemption moves forward.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with her request; the action comes last.

rute-pro-rute-05-capa-04.hint: The promise to act closes the sequence.

options.a: She asks for the redeemer's covering
options.b: He publicly recognizes her worth
